A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we have identified a set of genes that are dysregulated in obesity related NASH that are shared with fibrosis in other causes of cirhosis and that these genes can be used to identify patients with advanced NASH and to study the mechanisms of liver fibrosis in general.
obesity-related NASH is characterized by a unique gene expression profile that is distinct from that of NASH with normal liver histology, and also from other forms of advanced liver fibrosis.
the transcriptomic profiling of liver samples from NASH patients with inflammation and fibrotic lesions identified a core set of genes that are associated with the development of fibrosis.
The main takeaway from our work is that
we have identified a core set of genes that are dysregulated in NASH fibrosis, which are also dysregulated in fibrosis due to other causes.

there are a number of genes that are dysregulated in NASH that are not dysregulated in other types of liver disease, such as viral or alcoholic hepatitis, and this suggests that these genes could be important for understanding the pathogenesis of NASH.

there is a core set of genes associated with fibrosis that is common among multiple causes of cirrhogenesis, including obesity-related NASH, alcohol-related NASH, and hepatitis C virus-related cirrhosis.
